newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FLY-HALVES SHUFFLE PRELUDES FRENCH SEASON.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FLY-HALVES SHUFFLE PRELUDES FRENCH SEASON.

text.p: A close-season shuffle of fly-halves has resulted in some new look line-ups for French rugby union's league season which kicks off this weekend.

While recruitment of internationals has been low key in comparison with England, two tested World Cup fly-halves in Lisandro Arbizu of Argentina and Italy's Diego Dominguez have been snapped up as French clubs come to terms with the workings of the professional system.
Arbizu, who captained the Pumas in their recent series against England and New Zealand, has joined European Cup holders Brive who open the championship at home against Dax on Friday night.
Dominguez has left his adopted homeland after nearly 10 years with Milan to become one of a large clutch of signings made by newly-promoted Stade Francais.
The club has also signed two high quality locks in New Zealander Grant Ross from Brive and former France captain Olivier Roumat from Dax.

Champions Toulouse, the first European Cup winners two seasons ago, have signed Yann Delaigue from Toulon as understudy to veteran fly-half Christophe Deylaud, who at 32 has hinted he is not far away from retirement.

Another former French international number 10, Didier Camberabero, has returned to Beziers after four years spent at Nimes and Grenoble while Castres have coaxed rising star Thomas Castaignede from Toulouse where he was generally a centre.
One fly-half who remained loyal to his club was Dax's versatile Richard Dourthe, who has played at centre, wing and full-back for France. He turned down an offer from Brive.

Former France coach Pierre Berbizier is back at Narbonne as manager but he failed to prevent international prop Franck Tournaire leaving for Toulouse, whose 24 million francs ($4.8 million) budget gives them strong recruiting power.
French Cup winners Pau are looking for another good season among the championship favourites with international hooker Jean Michel Gonzalez, who has joined from Bayonne, strengthening their pack.
The championship, due to be reduced from 20 to 16 clubs next season, is divided into two pools of 10 sides each with the top four in each qualifying for the quarter-finals in April.
It starts with three consecutive weekends in August, then breaks for three months until late November to enable clubs to concentrate on European competition, which is gaining in importance each year.
"From the start of the season we are going to give priority to the European Cup," Toulouse coach Guy Noves said after his side failed to retain the trophy last season.
